source.authors: Ohno M, Yamawo A.
source.title: Night interruption provides evidence for photoperiodic regulation of bud burst in Japanese beech, Fagus crenata.

where: Materials and methods; Results and discussion; Figures 1–2
quote: The photoperiod interruption treatments demonstrated that F. crenata perceives night length during photoperiodic regulation of bud burst.
method: Twigs from nine trees, four lighting regimes at 20 °C; night-interrupted and short-day groups had equal total daily light
note: Full-source upgrade over earlier abstract record. Night interruption accelerated budburst versus uninterrupted short day (P<.001); functional photoperiod perception, not a measured pigment spectrum.

source.title: Endophytic Bacterial Exopolysaccharide and Ethylene Hyperactivate Flavonoid Synthesis in Leaves of <i>Fagus sylvatica</i> L. with False Heartwood.

quote: after 6 h, their flavonoid content increased by 38.7%
method: Fresh leaf exposure to 0.1% isolated bacterial EPS at 25 °C, water controls, spectrophotometric flavonoid assay
note: Response to a microbial macromolecular elicitor. Authors lack direct molecular proof of the proposed ethylene pathway; no receptor identity is asserted.

value: Leaves respond to 10 mM ethephon: flavonoids increase 21.9% by 4 h in false-heartwood morphotype, after an initial decline; normal-heartwood morphotype remains unreactive

source.authors: Likhanov A, Bilous S, Smetanska I, Kharkhota M, Subin O, Gryb V, Boroday V, Zelena L, Shevchuk M, Bilous A.
source.title: Endophytic Bacterial Exopolysaccharide and Ethylene Hyperactivate Flavonoid Synthesis in Leaves of <i>Fagus sylvatica</i> L. with False Heartwood.

quote: By the fourth hour, their total content increased by 21.9%.
method: In-vivo ethephon spray to wet leaf surfaces, sampling at 0–4 h, spectrophotometric flavonoid assay
note: Ethephon is an ethylene-releasing treatment. Record preserves the applied-compound response; ethephon alone does not isolate all effects of gaseous ethylene. No carry to F. grandifolia.

value: Radial stem growth occurs mainly at night; median diel growth peaks at 01:00 and reaches its minimum at 13:00 in the Swiss forest dataset

source.authors: Zweifel R, Sterck F, Braun S, Buchmann N, Eugster W, Gessler A, Häni M, Peters RL, Walthert L, Wilhelm M, Ziemińska K, Etzold S
source.title: Why trees grow at night

where: Results: Species-specific features; Figure 2d and Table 1
quote: Fagus sylvatica started to increase (13:00 h) and reached the peak (01:00 h) of its median diel growth earlier than all other species
method: Hourly analysis of high-resolution point-dendrometer measurements (2011–2018); authors’ zero-growth approach separates irreversible radial increments from reversible hydration changes
note: Directly reported species-level diel growth pattern. A free-running endogenous clock was not measured; the authors explicitly describe circadian control of growth as speculation. Dendrometer-based growth separation has methodological uncertainty discussed in the paper.
